question: Using usual notations for a completely randomised design with 'v' number of treatments and ‘n’ number of experimental units, the mean sum of squares due to treatments is calculated by:
solution:
The correct answer is** Sum of squares due to treatmentsv−1" id="MathJax-Element-487-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">Sum of squares due to treatmentsv−1Sum of squares due to treatmentsv−1
\rm \frac{Sum \ of\ squares\ due\ to\ treatments}{v-1}

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Mean Sum of Squares due to Treatments:

__
 
• Sum of Squares due to Treatments (SST) is the total variation explained by the treatments in the experiment.
